Goal: to explore National Unity Day and practise EGE Listening and Writing tasks

Vocabulary: history and celebrations

Listening: a dialogue about National Unity Day (EGE Listening task 2)

Writing: an informal email about National Unity Day (EGE Task 37)

• commemorate a historical event — to remember and show respect for an important event from the past
  • join forces — to work together with other people to achieve a shared goal
  • put on cultural events — to organise events such as concerts, festivals or exhibitions
  • take part in celebrations — to join activities or events organised for a special occasion
  • bring people together — to help people feel connected and develop stronger relationships
  • keep traditions alive — to continue practising traditions so that they are not forgotten

From: Oliver@mail.uk
To: Russian_friend@ege.ru
Subject: Public holidays

...We've been discussing public holidays at school and how they bring people together. Why do you think National Unity Day matters to young people in Russia? What would you recommend a tourist see or do on that day? Have you ever attended a National Unity Day event yourself?

...My classmates and I are organising a charity book fair at school next month...

Sample answer

Hello Oliver,

Thanks a lot for your email. Hope you're doing well!

You've asked about National Unity Day. I think it matters to many teenagers because it reminds us that people can achieve more when they join forces. If you visited Russia on National Unity Day, I'd recommend going to a concert or craft workshop, as lots of towns put on cultural events. As for me, I went to a local exhibition last year with my friends. We learnt about different regional traditions, which was surprisingly interesting.

Your school charity book fair sounds great! What kinds of books will be on sale at the fair? Who will receive the money raised at the charity book fair? Can people from outside the school come along?

Write back soon!

Yours, Alex
